paper_id: Reliable and efficient big service selection
title: Reliable and efficient big service selection
motivation: Big services face high QoS uncertainty and NP-hard selection time cost, making conventional methods inefficient.
problem_framing: Big service selection as bi-objective optimization: minimize time cost while maximizing reliability under global QoS constraints.
key_insight: Filter services by coefficient of variation to prune unreliable candidates, dramatically reducing the MIP search space.
method_signature: CVMIP: Coefficient of Variation filtering + Mixed Integer Programming
evaluation_criteria: Computation time, reliability fitness (CV-based), and near-to-optimal performance gap.
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: CVMIP achieves 92% optimality on average; the 8% gap is admitted but claimed imperceptible.
evidence_for_taste: QoS uncertainty of a big service can lower its service reliability
A big service with consistently good QoS is typically more reliable
the gap (8%) is very little and imperceptible
thinking_moves: Redefine reliability as low coefficient of variation (QoS consistency) rather than raw QoS values
Pre-filter unreliable services before optimization to shrink NP-hard search space
Accept near-optimality (92%) as sufficient when time cost and reliability gains are substantial
